limits: No tests, compiler, native calls or source edits by independent reviewer.
Official source semantics and cached C controls do not establish current macOS native ACL or installed boot acceptance.
No phase acceptance; root owns promotion and native CI qualification.
scope: Read-only independent source review of two cached Darwin ACL repairs
workerControls: Both before C controls exit 1; both patched controls exit 0 after successful C compilation. These are stubbed Linux controls, not Apple native execution.
Controls cover absent ACL, init/stat/query/extraction failure, NULL/remove sentinel, invalid ACL, deny/read-only allow/write allow, unknown tag and iterator/permission failures.
conclusions: Fresh filesec_init plus successful fstatx_np and successful FILESEC_ACL query distinguishes absent ACL from query/allocation failure. A failed or ambiguous query refuses.

FILESEC_ACL extraction allocates an independent acl_t via acl_copy_int_native and acl_init; acl_free releases that copy, while filesec_free releases its separate raw ACL buffer and container. No double free identified.
ACL validation, maximum entry bound, EINVAL-only iteration completion, private allow refusal, ancestor mutation mask and error refusal are preserved.
Mount locality and ownership checks remain intact; runtime retains root-owned APFS requirement and fixes only the incorrect ownership-ignore constant.
